title: Absolute faith is justification foundation and root (Jaubert/Arnold)
source_text: XVIII. Proinde fidem absolute spectatam, nempe, prout est assensus, movente Spiritu Sancto, toti Verbo Dei adhibitus, dicunt esse nostrae justificationis fundamentum & radicem; unde videlicet nostra coram Deo justitia incipere & veluti progerminare solet, & sine qua impossibile est ad eam pervenire; quamvis si in illo nudo assensu haereatur, nec charitas accedat, quae illum perficiat, fides ejusmodi non possit hominem ad justitiam & salutem perducere. Non secus ac fundamentum est principium domus, & id quod ad illius aedificationem primo & praecipue requiritur; sed tamen ut fiat domus ad habitationem, necesse est accedant parietes & tectum, sine quibus positum fundamentum nullius est usus. Quod sic verbis Arnoldi Jesuitae docet Jaubertus Arelatensis Archiepiscopus. Quamvis, inquit, in Ecclesia Catholica teneamus impossibile esse sine vera fide Deo placere, & esse justum, & fidem esse radicem arboris, & fundamentum domus: nihilominus si fides non sit per charitatem operans, domus est sine tecto, & arbor sine fructu, quorum neutrum quicquam Domino suo prodest. Adversus Molinaei Clypeum, Tom. 1. c. 40. num. 5.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore they say faith absolutely considered, namely assent, the Holy Spirit moving, applied to the whole Word of God, is the foundation and root of our justification, from which our justice before God begins and as it were sprouts, and without which it is impossible to arrive at it; yet if one sticks in that bare assent and charity does not come to perfect it, such faith cannot lead a person to justice and salvation. Just as a foundation is the principle of a house and what is first required for building it, yet walls and a roof must be added for a dwelling, otherwise the laid foundation is of no use. Jaubert of Arles teaches this in Arnold the Jesuit words: although in the Catholic Church we hold it impossible to please God and be just without true faith, and that faith is the root of the tree and foundation of the house, nevertheless if faith does not work through charity, the house is without a roof and the tree without fruit, neither of which profits its Lord (Against Molinaeus Shield, Tom. 1, c. 40, n. 5).
pass_b_english: Rome therefore calls absolute faith, Spirit-moved assent to the whole Word, justification foundation and root: from it justice before God begins to sprout, and without it no one reaches justice.

Yet bare assent without charity cannot carry anyone to justice or salvation, any more than a foundation without walls and roof makes a house; Jaubert via Arnold says faith without charity-working is a roofless house and fruitless tree (Adv. Molinaei Clypeum 1.40.5).

lemmas.gloss: the house is without a roof, and the tree without fruit

choices.why: Roman metaphor for absolute faith before charity forms it.
